data.question: I'm brand new to Obsidian. Is this too advanced?
data.answer: Not at all. OSK is designed for **beginners**. The user guide explains everything step by step, and the Getting Started Roadmap tells you what to learn first. Many people start with OSK on their very first day with `Obsidian`.

data.question: What's new in v5?
data.answer: v5 brings everything that proved itself in my vault since v4 into yours: **finished work that files itself** (statuses stamp their dates, done actions archive after seven days), **one-click Quick Actions** on your daily note, **Activities and Ideas** in the action system, **time budgets and delivery stats**, refreshed templates and Bases with Kanban boards, new AI skills, agents that remember what they learn, and a **Claude Code setup that finds skills on demand** instead of loading all of them up front. Add nine new plugins (K-Plex, the Kanban Action Planner and the Knowii Community plugin among them) and a much more capable OSK plugin. Everything else (and there's a LOT) is in the [v5.0.0 release notes](https://notes.dsebastien.net/30+Areas/33+Permanent+notes/33.04+Creations/Products/Obsidian+Starter+Kit/Release+Notes/Obsidian+Starter+Kit+-+Release+Notes+-+v5.0.0).

data.question: I'm on v4. How do I upgrade to v5?
data.answer: You don't start over. The [v4 to v5 migration guide](https://notes.dsebastien.net/30+Areas/33+Permanent+notes/33.04+Creations/Products/Obsidian+Starter+Kit/Migration+Guides/Obsidian+Starter+Kit+-+Migration+Guide+-+v4.x+to+v5.0.0) takes you through it step by step and tells you what to merge where you customized the kit. Back up your vault first: on its first launch, v5 archives finished actions older than seven days.

data.question: What do I need to run it?
data.answer: `Obsidian` **1.13.7 or newer** (several bundled plugins need a recent version). The AI part is optional; for it, you need an AI coding agent such as `Claude Code`, and the skills that run scripts also need `bun`. Everything else works without any of it.

data.question: Which AI tools does it work with?
data.answer: `Claude Code` gets everything: the `MCP` servers, on-demand skill search, the slash commands, the output styles and every safety hook. `Codex` gets the `MCP` servers and the hooks. `Gemini CLI` gets the hooks (you add the `MCP` servers yourself). `GitHub Copilot` in your IDE reads the vault rules and the skill files.

data.question: Where do I download v5?
data.answer: Where you bought the kit: your Gumroad library, or the Obsidian Starter Kit space in Knowii if you got it through the community. [learn.knowii.net](https://learn.knowii.net) explains both.

data.question: Won't AI just fill my vault with generic content?
data.answer: That's exactly what OSK is designed to prevent. The kit is built on a clear **AI Augmentation Philosophy**: AI augments your thinking; it never replaces it. The **identity layer** calibrates AI to your voice, values, and goals. **LLM Wikis** track sources and confidence for every claim. **Pre-publish review panels** (Editor, Skeptic, Hater, Beginner, Power User) catch generic output before it ships. AI handles the busywork; you stay the author. You can outsource the labor; you can't outsource your understanding.

data.question: Do I need AI tools to use OSK?
data.answer: No. OSK works great as a "classic" PKM system, and the user guide shows what to switch off if you want AI out of your vault entirely. When you're ready for AI, everything is already wired: agents, AI skills, LLM Wikis, an identity layer, and the OSK plugin (CLI + `MCP` server) that helps AI tools understand your whole vault. `Claude Code` and `Codex` connect to it on first launch.

data.question: I already have an Obsidian vault, or an older version of OSK. Can I migrate?
data.answer: Yes. Each major version of OSK comes with a step-by-step migration guide; the latest one takes you from v4 to v5 and keeps your setup. Starting from a vault of your own? Open OSK next to it and bring your notes in at your own pace; the user guide explains where each kind of note goes.

data.question: What if OSK doesn't fit my workflow?
data.answer: OSK is a starting point, not a straitjacket. **Everything is customizable**. Tweak the structure, templates, and plugins to match how you think. And if it's really not right for you, there's a **30-day money-back guarantee**.

data.question: How do updates work?
data.answer: **Every update is free, for life**, v5 and every version after it included. You download new versions where you bought the kit: your Gumroad library, or the Obsidian Starter Kit space in Knowii. I announce every release by email, and the release notes document every change.

data.question: Do I need to pay for Obsidian?
data.answer: No. `Obsidian` is **free**, including for work (the commercial license is optional). OSK is a pre-built vault plus documentation; the two are separate products.

data.question: Is support included?
data.answer: Yes. Email me your questions; I answer them myself and help people get started. If you're a [Knowii Community](/product/knowii-community) member, you can also ask there, right inside Obsidian with the Knowii Community plugin.

data.question: Can I use OSK for work or commercial purposes?
data.answer: Absolutely. Consultants, project managers and knowledge workers use OSK for their professional work. `Obsidian` itself is free for work too (the commercial license is optional).

data.question: What's the difference between Essentials and Premium?
data.answer: **Essentials** (**${product.variants.0.price|currency}**) includes the complete vault, the online user guide and every future update. **Premium** (**${product.variants.1.price|currency}**) adds the **2h20m** Obsidian Starter Course, a video course on `Obsidian` and PKM fundamentals. Both are one-time purchases with free updates for life.
